summary.en: Compare auto, register, static and extern using duration, visibility and linkage.
summary.bn: auto, register, static ও extern দিয়ে ভেরিয়েবলের স্থায়িত্ব ও ফাইলের মধ্যে সংযোগ বোঝো।

notes: This lesson uses C17 storage-class rules; C23 additionally permits auto type inference in certain declarations.

sections.title: Storage class is more than a location label
A static initializer is not a repeated reset

examples.title: Spell out auto and register
examples.explanationHtml: The sum is 10. register changes neither the loop arithmetic nor the promised storage location.

examples.title: A local static counts calls
examples.explanationHtml: The zero-initialized static visits object is shared across these calls, giving 1 and then 2.

examples.title: Internal linkage for a private total
examples.explanationHtml: Both the helper and total are private names within this translation unit. The two amounts still accumulate into one object.

examples.title: extern refers to a later definition
examples.explanationHtml: The declaration reserves no second object. The definition below main provides the storage initialized to 60.

practice.title: Static running sum
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 to 8 followed by n integers from -100 to 100. A function adds each to a local static sum and returns it. Print Count and amounts: then each running sum on a separate line.
hints: Only the function owns the persistent total.

practice.title: Count only accepted readings
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 1 to 8 followed by n readings from -20 to 100. A function increments a local static count for nonnegative readings only. Print Readings: then the final count.
hints: Return the count after deciding whether to increment it.

practice.title: Private stock object
practice.statementHtml: Read a sale quantity from 0 to 20. Use a file-scope static stock initialized to 20 and a static sell helper. Print Sale: then remaining stock.
hints: File-scope static affects linkage, not whether writes are allowed.

practice.title: Use an extern rate declaration
practice.statementHtml: Read units from 0 to 100. Declare extern int rate before main and define rate = 7 after main. Print Units: then units times rate.

quiz.prompt: Which C17 block declaration uses the default automatic class explicitly?
quiz.explanation: auto explicitly names the usual block-variable storage class; it is normally omitted.

quiz.prompt: What does register guarantee about physical storage?
quiz.explanation: register is a hint and does not force a machine register.

quiz.prompt: A static local starts at 10 and gains two per call. Which values appear?
quiz.explanation: The initializer runs once; the stored value advances from ten to twelve to fourteen.

quiz.prompt: Which operation is forbidden on a C17 register int object?
options: Using it as a loop counter
quiz.explanation: The language forbids the address operator even if the compiler does not use a physical register.

quiz.prompt: What does static at file scope usually change for an object name?
options: It changes duration from automatic to static
quiz.explanation: File-scope objects already have static duration; static gives the name internal linkage.

quiz.prompt: An explicit auto subtotal is rebuilt for each call. Which totals are printed?
quiz.explanation: Each call creates a fresh automatic total initialized to three.

quiz.prompt: Which line normally declares a shared object without defining its storage?
quiz.explanation: An extern declaration without an initializer refers to a definition elsewhere. An initialized declaration is a definition.

quiz.prompt: Where should an initialized externally linked object usually be defined?
options: Inside every caller block with extern
quiz.explanation: Use one definition and share a compatible extern declaration through a header.

quiz.prompt: An extern declaration refers to the definition below main. What rate is printed?
quiz.explanation: The compatible declaration and definition identify one initialized object.

quiz.prompt: What is the initial value of an uninitialized static int?
quiz.explanation: Static-duration arithmetic objects are zero-initialized before normal execution.

quiz.prompt: Can a local static initializer call a helper at runtime in C17?
options: Only if the helper returns int
No, it needs a permitted constant initializer
quiz.explanation: C static initialization does not provide first-call function evaluation like some other languages.

quiz.prompt: Does adding an initializer to extern int rate make it a definition?
quiz.explanation: An initialized object declaration supplies a definition even with extern written.

keyPoints.en: auto is the default storage class for ordinary block variables.
keyPoints.bn: সাধারণ ব্লক ভেরিয়েবলে ডিফল্ট স্টোরেজ ক্লাস auto।

keyPoints.en: register is a hint and does not promise a CPU register.
keyPoints.bn: register একটি পরামর্শ; CPU রেজিস্টার ব্যবহারের নিশ্চয়তা নয়।

keyPoints.en: A local static object keeps its value between calls.
keyPoints.bn: লোকাল static ভেরিয়েবলের মান কলের মাঝেও থাকে।

keyPoints.en: A file-scope static name has internal linkage.
keyPoints.bn: ফাইল স্কোপে static নাম একই সোর্স ফাইলের মধ্যে সীমিত।

keyPoints.en: An extern declaration can refer to a definition elsewhere.
keyPoints.bn: extern ঘোষণা অন্য জায়গায় সংজ্ঞায়িত ভেরিয়েবলকে বোঝাতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: C17 forbids taking the address of a register object.
keyPoints.bn: C17-এ register ভেরিয়েবলের অ্যাড্রেস নেওয়া যায় না।

examQuestions.question: Compare static inside a function with static at file scope, and state the role of extern.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A static local has block scope, no linkage and static duration. A file-scope static object has static duration and internal linkage. An ordinary extern declaration can refer to one compatible definition elsewhere; it does not create another initialized object.

#include <stdio.h>

int next(void)
{
    static int value = 10;
    value += 2;
    return value;
}

int main(void)
{
    printf("%d\n", next());
    printf("%d\n", next());
    return 0;
}

12
14

The initializer runs once; the stored value advances from ten to twelve to fourteen.

examQuestions.question: Read units from 0 to 100. Declare extern int rate before main and define rate = 7 after main. Print Units: then units times rate.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>
extern int rate;
int main(void)
{
    int units;
    puts("Units:");
    if (scanf("%d", &units) != 1 || units < 0 || units > 100) {
        return 1;
    }
    printf("%d\n", units * rate);
    return 0;
}
int rate = 7;

Keep exactly one initialized definition.

For input 0, the program prints:

Units:
0
